title: K8s edge bootstrap and ops playbook — baremetal + vSphere (terraform sketch)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for bootstrapping and operating on-prem Kubernetes clusters used for Redwood Private deployments. Focus is on two common environments we support: bare-metal racks (PXE/IPMI) and vSphere (vCenter-managed workload clusters). The goal is a single, repeatable path to a prod-like cluster for testing and customer air-gapped installs, plus a Terraform module sketch and an upgrade plan.

Audience
- Platform/Infra engineers running Private installations
- Solutions engineers preparing customer installs
- SREs responsible for upgrades and rollback

Scope and constraints
- Target K8s versions: 1.26 -> 1.27 upgrade window for next quarter (adjustable)
- Networking: Calico (BGP for baremetal), Antrea (overlay on vSphere) — recommend isolating control-plane network from tenant traffic
- Storage: CSI driver mapping notes later in doc. Prefer Ceph/Rook for baremetal; VMFS/VMware VVols for vSphere.
- Security: assume customer owns KMS/HSM for private installs.

High-level cluster types
1) Edge/Baremetal (PXE -> Ignition / kubeadm + cri-dockerd or containerd):
   - BMC/IPMI provisioning using iPXE -> CoreOS/Flatcar or Ubuntu minimal image with ignition templates.
   - Control plane nodes SSD-backed, separate etcd disks on local NVMe when possible.
   - BGP peering to on-prem network using Calico (ASNs per rack).

2) vSphere (vCenter managed):
   - VM templates (cloud-init) for masters/workers, use vSphere CPI + external CCM where required.
   - Use vSphere storage classes, HA via vCenter HA and DRS.

Bootstrap sequence (high level)
- PRECHECKS (manual/automated): k8s version matrix, IP pools, DNS entries, BMC credentials inventory, vCenter template versions, NTP sync, KMS access verified.
- Provision infrastructure: (1) baremetal: PXE boot images; (2) vSphere: create VMs from templates via Terraform provider.
- Install OS + base packages: containerd, cri, kubelet (pinned), kubeadm binary, iptables, tc, nvme tools.
- Bootstrap control plane with kubeadm init (or use cluster API for vSphere flows). Enable kube-proxy, CoreDNS.
- Apply CNI (Calico/Antrea) and check Pod networking.
- Join worker nodes.
- Deploy Redwood operator (private deployment agent), ingress controller, monitoring stack (Prometheus node exporter), and PVCs for logging.

Commands / snippets (conceptual)
- kubeadm init --config=/etc/kubeadm/config.yaml --upload-certs
- kubeadm join <CONTROL_PLANE_IP>:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>
- terraform apply -var 'vcenter_user=svc-redwood' -var 'cluster_name=customer-edge-01'
- ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC> -U admin -P <pw> chassis bootdev pxe

Terraform module notes (sketch)
- module "k8s_node_pool":
  - inputs: node_count, vm_template, cpu, memory, disk_size, labels, taints, network_id
  - outputs: node_ips, node_names, ssh_fingerprint
- module "baremetal_bmc":
  - inputs: bmc_inventory_csv (or API endpoint), provisioning_vlan, ipxe_script_url
  - outputs: provisioning_jobs (IDs)
- module "vcenter_cluster":
  - inputs: datacenter, cluster, resource_pool, datastore, template_map
  - outputs: vm_objects, vm_ids
- module "kubeadm_bootstrap":
  - inputs: control_plane_count, kubeadm_config_yaml (interpolated), certs_secret_id
  - outputs: kubeconfig_path
Notes:
- Keep modules small and composable. Module responsibilities: instantiate infra resources only. Don’t run bootstrap scripts that mutate cluster state except for controlled 'provisioner' module run.
- Secrets: store TF state in customer-controlled backend (consul/remote S3) and use KMS for encryption. Document in module README.

Upgrade plan (control plane + workers) — draft
Assumptions: minor version upgrade (1.26.x -> 1.27.y), control-plane N=3 for HA, rolling upgrade with zero tolerated downtime target.
1) Verify cluster health and baselines: ci-e2e smoke, metrics, PVs healthy.
2) Snapshot etcd (if external etcd) or create etcd backup using etcdctl snapshot save. Push snapshot to secure location.
3) Drain and upgrade nodes one at a time (control-plane first if running stacked etcd):
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m
   - Upgrade kubeadm/kubelet binaries on node (package repo pinned in TF or image template for vSphere)
   - kubeadm upgrade node
   - systemctl restart kubelet; kubectl uncordon <node>
4) After control-plane finished, perform same on worker pools.

Fast rollback plan (if upgrade causes regressions):
- If app-level regressions: route traffic to standby region or fallback model in Redwood router (if available).
- If control-plane fails: restore from etcd snapshot to a new cluster with same API server certs (documented recovery steps).
- Keep the previous TF state snapshot and images pinned so a rollback can reprovision older VMs quickly.

Operational checklists (daily / before customer handoff)
- Node disk < 75% used
- CPU/mem saturation < 70% on control-plane nodes
- CoreDNS latency < 50ms p95
- All PVs bound, CSI controller ready

Troubleshooting notes and gotchas
- Baremetal NIC naming drift: prefer label by MAC to avoid netplan/udev renaming mismatches.
- vSphere: storage policy mismatches cause PVC binding delays — ensure default storageclass exists.
- Calico BGP: mis-configured ASNs cause cross-rack traffic blackholes — always validate BGP session up via bird/ calicoctl node status.
- kube-proxy vs iptables: when using external firewall/iptables changes, double-check conntrack settings for large scale deployments.

Open questions / TODOs (explicit):
- Decide single recommended CNI for both environments vs two CNIs maintenance overhead. (decision owner: @Evan)
- Merge strategy for TF modules into redwood-infra repo: keep separate customer modules or unified? (RFC needed).
- Automated validation harness: add a CI job that runs the full bootstrap flow in VMware lab for every TF PR.

Appendix: useful links and commands
- etcd backup example: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 snapshot save /tmp/etcd-20241014.db --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key
- quick health: kubectl get cs; kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl get pods -A | egrep "CrashLoopBackOff|ImagePullBackOff"
- Helpful Jira/PRs: INFOPS-4387, GH PR #72 (infra/terraform-modules)

Notes to self: this doc needs a tighter set of runbook steps for restore-from-snapshot and a small diagram for network flows. Also iterate with Solutions team to collect customer-specific constraints (airgap, KMS, firewall rules).

End of draft.
